findings.title: Retain native descendant cleanup when resource caps are omitted
findings.body: AC2.2, AC2.5 and T2's ownership-preservation constraint are violated by skipping `setup_cgroup` for no-resource and FD-only requests. On a delegated runner, the baseline still placed those launches into an owned leaf; the new branch always chooses `Cleanup::None`. A native T2 executable launched through `spawn_and_bridge` can fork a descendant (`linux.rs` permits `clone`/`execve`), after which dropping/finalizing the bridge only kills/reaps its direct child: the only descendant-wide kill is `Cleanup::Cgroup::drop` (`sandbox/mod.rs:109-135`), which this branch disables. Descendants can therefore outlive the owning launch, or keep the bridge's reader joins waiting if they inherit stdout/stderr. Preserve best-effort owned placement/cleanup even without CPU/memory/PID limits, while keeping unavailable delegation nonfatal and emitting no resource-downgrade row for these requests; add the same descendant-teardown control with empty/FD-only caps. This is established from the changed branch and its actual cleanup consumer; no runtime reproduction was executed during review.

findings.title: Exercise native above-hard FD refusal and owned-leaf cleanup
findings.body: Missing acceptance evidence, not an observed limit-enforcement defect: AC1.2 requires a bounded above-hard `RLIMIT_NOFILE` refusal with no guest execution and released owned resources for native T2 as well as T3. The replacement failure smoke exercises creation, limit-write and exec failures, but neither it nor the full admitted-session suite includes this native case; the actual above-hard control in `worker_resource_limits_17_2.rs` only exercises the rootless T3 runtime. Consequently the recorded native4/session22 passes do not establish native pre-exec FD-refusal cleanup or absence of a successful downgrade for that failure. Add an isolated native T2 within-hard control and an above-hard request under a deliberately lowered inherited hard nofile limit, assert the specific refusal/no guest effects/no downgrade and no owned leaf, and archive its capable-runner execution; the production `setrlimit` call alone is not that evidence.

findings.title: Uncapped native T2 launches lose descendant lifetime containment
findings.summary: A consumer launching a hostile native executable through spawn_sandboxed or spawn_and_bridge on a host with working cgroup delegation now loses process-tree cleanup when CPU, memory and PID requests are absent, including FD-only launches. The new cgroup_requested branch selects Cleanup::None, whereas the baseline attempted per-spawn cgroup placement even without resource ceilings. The child can use permitted clone/clone3 to create a descendant before its leader exits or is stopped. Native teardown kills/reaps only the leader; the skipped cgroup guard was the mechanism that killed remaining members. [INFERENCE] Descendants can consequently survive unload/revocation and continue consuming resources. Retaining an otherwise idle stdout/stderr pipe can also indefinitely block bridge teardown while it joins reader threads. This is a cap-independent weakening of the exposed native sandbox boundary, not a demonstrated escape through a pure WASM guest or the T3 Worker route.

locations.role: New bypass of per-spawn cgroup placement and ownership
T2 permits execve and clone; clone3 is also permitted at line 332
Native guard kills/reaps only its immediate child
Skipped cgroup guard supplies process-tree termination
Bridge synchronously joins pipe readers after immediate-child teardown

evidence.label: New cap-independent cleanup bypass
evidence.explanation: The baseline side of the exact diff called setup_cgroup(spec) unconditionally. The changed side skips it for no-resource and FD-only requests, even when delegation is available.

evidence.label: Credible native execution path
evidence.explanation: spawn_child routes Linux T2 BridgeSpawnSpec requests into spawn_sandboxed at runtime.rs:593-596. The native T2 allow-list contains unrestricted clone/clone3 and execve. A descendant remains confined by inherited Landlock/seccomp, but those controls do not terminate it when its parent exits.

evidence.label: Immediate-child teardown does not contain descendants
evidence.explanation: SandboxedChild::drop kills and waits only the Child PID. Cleanup::Cgroup additionally writes cgroup.kill, but Cleanup::None performs no equivalent tree-wide action. SpawnedBridge::drop then joins stdout/stderr readers, which can remain blocked if a surviving descendant holds the write ends.

evidence.label: Added regression does not cover the bypass
evidence.explanation: killed_leader_cleanup_kills_its_surviving_descendant uses caps(), whose CPU, memory and PID fields are all Some. The no-resource/FD-only session tests check successful execution and absence of downgrade rows, not descendant termination. This is source coverage evidence, not a claim that any test passed.

findings.remediation: Keep native lifetime containment independent from requested resource ceilings. Preserve owned per-launch cgroup placement/cleanup on delegated hosts for no-resource and FD-only T2 launches without inventing a memory-downgrade event when no memory ceiling was requested; preserve the existing documented undelegated policy. Extend the bounded descendant-cleanup regression to both cases, including a descendant retaining bridge pipes. Parent should reproduce and verify these cases after integration.

deferred.reason: Runtime reproduction and verification belong to the parent under the no-execution review contract. The surviving finding is grounded in the changed branch and existing process-creation/teardown controls; its runtime effects are explicitly identified as inference.

findings.title: Preserve descendant cleanup for native spawns without cgroup caps
findings.body: For a delegated Linux native T2 spawn with no CPU/memory/PID cap (including FD-only requests), this new branch unconditionally selects `Cleanup::None`; the baseline still created an owned cgroup when delegation was available. `SandboxedChild::drop` only kills/reaps the leader, and the only descendant-kill operation is `Cleanup::Cgroup`'s `cgroup.kill`, so a descendant survives leader crash, unload, or error cleanup on this newly bypassed path. A descendant retaining bridge stdout/stderr additionally leaves `SpawnedBridge::drop` blocked in its reader joins (`runtime.rs:1109-1118`). The new `killed_leader_cleanup_kills_its_surviving_descendant` regression covers only `caps()` with all cgroup resources requested, not this branch. Preserve tree-cleanup ownership independently of requested resource ceilings, or retain an unconfigured owned cgroup when delegation is available. This failure follows from source/ownership tracing; it was not executed during this review.
